events.title: Ruby 2.0 released
events.summary: Ruby 2.0.0 shipped on February 24, 2013 with keyword arguments, refinements, and significant performance improvements.
events.about: Ruby 2.0 refined the language Matz had been evolving since 1.9: mandatory keyword args cleaned up APIs; refinements scoped monkey patches safely; the VM got faster garbage collection. It powered Rails 4-era apps through the mid-2010s.

narrative.whyChosen: Ruby 2.0 was the stable baseline for Rails and Rubygems through the framework boom.
narrative.whyImportant: Keyword arguments and performance kept Ruby competitive with Python and Node.
narrative.problemSolved: Ruby 1.9's transition pain needed a polished 2.x line for production adoption.

events.title: Surface Pro released
events.summary: Microsoft began selling the Surface Pro on February 9, 2013 — a Windows 8 tablet with an Intel CPU and detachable keyboard cover.
events.about: The Surface Pro ran full desktop Windows and Visual Studio — Microsoft's bet that developers wanted tablet portability without an iOS/Android sandbox. Pen input and the Type Cover blurred laptop and tablet categories. It validated 2-in-1 hardware for Windows developers before Apple's iPad Pro added trackpad support.

narrative.whyChosen: The Surface Pro was Microsoft's flagship Windows tablet for developers and power users.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved Windows could ship on premium tablet hardware with active pen and keyboard accessories.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers wanted tablet portability but needed full Win32 and desktop IDEs, not just mobile apps.
